story: Robots assemble solar tables at Tormes Solar, Navarro County

claims.text: Matrix Renewables is deploying Terabase Energy's Terafab V2 automated solar construction platform at its 457 MW Tormes Solar project in Navarro County, Texas.
claims.quote: Spain-based independent power producer (IPP) Matrix Renewables is deploying Terafab V2, an automated solar construction platform developed by US-based Terabase Energy, at part of its 457 MW Tormes Solar project in Navarro County, Texas.

claims.text: Tormes Solar will be a 457 MWdc photovoltaic facility in Navarro County, Texas.
claims.quote: When commissioned, Tormes Solar will be a 457MWdc photovoltaic solar facility located in Navarro County, approximately two miles southeast of Barry and west of Corsicana.

claims.text: The system's robots fasten photovoltaic modules onto long rotating steel tracker torque tubes.
claims.quote: The system's robots fasten the photovoltaic modules onto long rotating steel tubes, called tracker torque tubes

claims.text: After assembly, AI-assisted tools perform quality checks to confirm everything is correctly placed.
claims.quote: Once the automated system has completed assembly of the finished units, it uses AI-assisted tools to perform quality checks, confirming everything is correctly placed.

claims.text: After inspection, robotic equipment loads the assemblies onto autonomous vehicles called rovers that carry them to locations in the solar field.
claims.quote: Following inspection, robotic equipment loads the completed assemblies onto autonomous vehicles, known as rovers, which transport them to designated locations in the solar field.

claims.text: Workers unload the assemblies and install them onto prepositioned tracker supports, a step that still requires people.
claims.quote: Workers then unload the assemblies and install them onto prepositioned tracker supports. ... the final installation of the assembled PV tables onto tracker supports still requires workers.

claims.text: Terabase says a single Terafab V2 line runs a two minute cycle time.
claims.quote: A single line achieves 2-minute cycle times that, running 24/7 around the clock, translate to more than 20 megawatts installed per week, or roughly 1 gigawatt per factory per year.

claims.text: Terabase says each line could produce around 20 MW per week under continuous operation.
claims.quote: According to the company, each line could achieve an output of around 20 MW per week under continuous operating conditions.

claims.text: SOLV Energy is the EPC contractor for Tormes Solar.
claims.quote: Matrix Renewables, the TPG Rise-backed global renewable platform, and EPC contractor SOLV Energy announced construction started on the Tormes Solar Project, marked by a groundbreaking ceremony on May 19.

claims.text: During construction Tormes Solar is expected to support approximately 450 jobs.
claims.quote: During construction, Tormes Solar is expected to support approximately 450 jobs.

claims.text: Tormes Solar is expected to begin commercial operations in the first half of 2027.
claims.quote: The portfolio includes the 457 MW Tormes Solar, under construction in Navarro County, Texas, expected to begin commercial operations in the first half of 2027.

claims.text: Terafab V2 is currently optimized for First Solar Series 7 modules and Nextpower trackers.
claims.quote: It is currently optimized for First Solar Series 7 modules and Nextpower trackers, although Terabase plans to expand compatibility with other module and tracker technologies.

claims.text: The site is about two miles southeast of Barry and west of Corsicana.
claims.quote: located in Navarro County, approximately two miles southeast of Barry and west of Corsicana.

claims.text: Terafab is deployed on only a portion of the 457 MWdc project, as a proof of concept for 24/7 automated solar construction.
claims.quote: The deployment at Tormes Solar represents a pioneering proof of concept for 24/7 automated solar construction. The technology is being deployed on a portion of the 457 MWdc project

claims.text: Tormes is the first deployment of Terafab V2 with autonomous rovers.
claims.quote: the company is deploying the next-gen Terafab® (V2) with autonomous rovers for the first time, exploring the potential for automated, AI-driven, around-the-clock solar construction.

claims.text: Terabase says the latest version of the on-site factory can be moved and set up in about four hours.
claims.quote: Terabase says the latest version can be moved and set up in approximately four hours, allowing the assembly line to be repositioned as construction progresses.

claims.text: In conventional construction workers attach heavy glass panels to field-installed torque tubes one by one, and Terafab inverts that by pre-assembling modules onto the tubes with in-line quality control on every unit.
claims.quote: In conventional solar construction, steel torque tubes are installed in the field first, and workers then manually attach hundreds of thousands of heavy glass solar panels to them one by one. Terafab inverts that process: modules are pre-assembled onto tracker torque tubes with in-line quality control verifying every unit, so defects are caught immediately.

claims.text: Terabase says the system eliminates manual lifting of heavy steel and glass components.
claims.quote: The system eliminates manual lifting of heavy steel and glass components, improving jobsite safety and enabling sustained operations in extreme heat.

claims.text: A manufacturing execution system coordinates assembly, material flows, inspections and transport, alongside a digital twin of the site.
claims.quote: Terafab V2 incorporates a manufacturing execution system (MES) to coordinate assembly operations, material flows, quality inspections and transportation. The platform also integrates construction planning, inventory management and logistics software with a digital twin of the project site.

claims.text: Terabase claims its approach can double labor productivity versus conventional installation, with actual output depending on site conditions.
claims.quote: The company claims its automated construction approach can double labor productivity compared with conventional utility-scale PV installation methods. Actual output depends on project configuration, equipment utilization and site conditions.

claims.text: The first-generation Terafab installed about 40 MW of tracker-mounted capacity across several US projects.
claims.quote: Terabase said the first-generation Terafab platform had been used to install approximately 40 MW of tracker-mounted solar capacity across several US projects.

claims.text: In 2022 Terabase used its technology to install 10 MW at a 400 MW solar project in central Texas.
claims.quote: Earlier that year, it had deployed its technology to install 10 MW of capacity at a 400 MW solar project in central Texas.

claims.text: Terabase is developing additional robotics to automate the final installation step in a future version.
claims.quote: Terabase has said it is developing additional robotics to automate this step in a future version of the platform.

claims.text: Terabase Energy is headquartered in Berkeley, California.
claims.quote: Headquartered in Berkeley, California, Terabase is backed by more than $200 million from SoftBank, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Prelude Ventures, Fifth Wall, SJF Ventures, EDP Ventures and others.

claims.text: Tormes Solar represents over $750 million in total investment.
claims.quote: The facility will represent over $750million in total investment in renewable energy infrastructure, systems, and the surrounding community.

claims.text: Matrix COO Giora Salita said construction automation is one of the biggest opportunities to improve how utility scale solar is delivered.
claims.quote: Construction automation remains one of the biggest opportunities to disrupt and improve how utility scale solar projects are delivered," said Giora Salita, COO of Matrix Renewables.

claims.text: Terabase CEO Matt Campbell said every other industry that had to scale learned to industrialise and energy construction is next.
claims.quote: Every other industry that had to scale learned to industrialise, and energy construction is next," added Matt Campbell, CEO and Co-Founder of Terabase Energy.

claims.text: SOLV CEO George Hershman said the company has been exploring automation because its average project size keeps increasing.
claims.quote: Given that our average project size continues to increase alongside the demand for renewable power, we have been exploring automation across the full lifecycle of our projects," commented George Hershman, CEO, SOLV Energy.

claims.text: SOLV and Matrix previously built the 284 MWdc Stillhouse Solar project in Texas.
claims.quote: SOLV and Matrix previously collaborated on and recently commissioned the 284-MWDC Stillhouse Solar project in Texas.

cautions: Terafab covers only a portion of the 457 MW site as a proof of concept. Never say robots are building the whole farm.
Two minutes per assembly and 20 MW per week are Terabase claims under continuous 24/7 operation, not measured Tormes output.
Doubling labor productivity is a company claim and output depends on site conditions.
Rovers are described as autonomous; do not claim they are driverless at every moment.
First-generation total conflicts (40 MW per pv magazine vs 130+ MW on Terabase's page). Attribute or skip.
Commercial operation in first half of 2027 is 'expected', from financing coverage.
Workers still do the final placement. Never say there are no people on the site.
No acreage or homes-powered figure is sourced. Do not voice one.
